clues: This city lies in the east of the Netherlands, close to the border with Germany. The east edge of its built-up area touches that border line.
Winters in this city are less mild than in the rest of its land. Its inland spot, far from the sea, is the cause of that extra bite.
This place began as a small settlement in the Middle Ages. In 1325, it was granted full city rights, and it grew from there.
For two long centuries, cloth made this city great. In the 1700s and 1800s, it was a major hub of the cloth trade and cloth making.
The last factory for Polaroid film stands in this city. That lone plant is a strange, famed link to the old age of film.
